text: Deduction is where the exam separates candidates, so picture a scale of certainty. Must: the only possible explanation. The lights are off; they must have gone out. May, might or could: one of several possibilities: she may be in the library. And can't: impossible. He can't be in Jumla; I saw him in Kathmandu an hour ago. Notice: the opposite of deductive must is can't, not mustn't.
